packet.headline_seed: Trump hits out at Italy's Meloni after pushback on G7 photo claim
packet.description_seed: Trump said the Italian leader asked "over and over" for a picture at G7, after she said the US president "made-up" a story that she "begged" for a photo.

what: Trump hits out at Italy's Meloni after pushback on G7 photo claim

clean_source_blocks.text: Trump said the Italian leader asked "over and over" for a picture at G7, after she said the US president "made-up" a story that she "begged" for a photo.

US President Donald Trump has hit out at Italy's prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, repeating his claim that she asked "over and over" for a picture of them together at the G7 summit this week. In a post on Truth Social, Trump also accused her of not supporting US efforts to "[deny] Iran from obtaining or developing a nuclear weapon". He said that Meloni caused "a great logistical inconvenience" by barring the US from using Italian air facilities for American military operations in Iran. On Friday, the prime minister said she had been astonished by Trump's initial claim that she "begged" for a photo. In his post on Truth Social a day later, the US president said Meloni was "doing poorly in Italy with her level of popularity".

Italy's Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni looks on ahead of a working session at the G7 summit, in Evian-les-Bains, France, Wednesday, June 17, 2026. Credit: AP/Mandel Ngan ROME — The Italian government closed ranks on Friday to slam U.S. President Donald Trump over his claim that Premier Giorgia Meloni had “begged” for a photo with him during the recent G7 summit, a pushback that suggested America’s longtime European ally had had enough of Trump’s boasting and criticism. Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani abruptly cancelled a planned trip to the United States this weekend, calling Trump’s claims “serious and offensive” toward Meloni and all of Italy. The Foreign Ministry later announced that the business and scientific forum Tajani was to attend in Miami had also been called off.

But soon afterwards, Trump gave a phone interview with Italy's La7 TV channel in which he alleged: "She begged me to take a photo with her; I felt sorry for her." "She's probably happy I spoke to her," he said. La7 did not produce Trump's original words in English, but voiced them over in Italian. Responding to the claim, Meloni in an Instagram video said she was "frankly stunned". "I don't know why the US president behaves this way towards allies," she said, adding it was not the first time it had happened. "I can only say it is regrettable he does not show the same determination towards the enemies of the West and towards the enemies of the US - [enemies] whose leaders he instead appears to be far more accommodating with."

US President Donald Trump has hit out at Italy's prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, repeating his claim that she asked "over and over" for a picture of them together at the G7 summit this week.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump also accused her of not supporting US efforts to "[deny] Iran from obtaining or developing a nuclear weapon".

He said that Meloni caused "a great logistical inconvenience" by barring the US from using Italian air facilities for American military operations in Iran.

On Friday, the prime minister said she had been astonished by Trump's initial claim that she "begged" for a photo.

In his post on Truth Social a day later, the US president said Meloni was "doing poorly in Italy with her level of popularity".

"Now, after the United States defeated Iran militarily, she wants to be friends again in order to get her "numbers up." No thanks!!!," he added.

In March, Italy reportedly denied US military air craft from landing at Sigonella air base in Sicily for operations against Iran.

The continued exchange has highlighted a developing rift between the two countries since Trump's military action against Iran this year.

Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani has also cancelled a trip to the US early next week.

Trump and Meloni were pictured in close conversation at the G7 summit in France this week, and the Italian leader later told reporters their relationship was unchanged and there had been "no recriminations".

But soon afterwards, Trump gave a phone interview with Italy's La7 TV channel in which he alleged: "She begged me to take a photo with her; I felt sorry for her."

"She's probably happy I spoke to her," he said. La7 did not produce Trump's original words in English, but voiced them over in Italian.

Responding to the claim, Meloni in an Instagram video said she was "frankly stunned".

"I don't know why the US president behaves this way towards allies," she said, adding it was not the first time it had happened.

"I can only say it is regrettable he does not show the same determination towards the enemies of the West and towards the enemies of the US - [enemies] whose leaders he instead appears to be far more accommodating with."

"But there is one thing he needs to remember: neither I nor Italy ever beg."

Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani abruptly cancelled a planned trip to the United States this weekend, calling Trump’s claims “serious and offensive” toward Meloni and all of Italy. The Foreign Ministry later announced that the business and scientific forum Tajani was to attend in Miami had also been called off.

Meloni for her part posted a video calling Trump’s claims “completely fabricated" and expressing astonishment that he would invent such things about an ally.

payload.title: Trumpin ja Melonin kiista G7-kuvasta kiristyi
payload.summary: Yhdysvaltain presidentti Donald Trump ja Italian pääministeri Giorgia Meloni ovat ajautuneet julkiseen sanaharkkaan G7-huippukokouksessa otetuksi väitetystä yhteiskuvasta.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltain presidentti Donald Trump on jatkanut arvosteluaan Italian pääministeriä Giorgia Melonia kohtaan sen jälkeen, kun Meloni torjui Trumpin väitteen, jonka mukaan hän olisi pyytänyt toistuvasti yhteiskuvaa G7-huippukokouksessa. Kiista on laajentunut valokuvaväitteestä Italian hallituksen ja Yhdysvaltain presidentin väliseksi diplomaattiseksi yhteenotoksi.

## Kiista alkoi valokuvaväitteestä

Trump väitti ensin italialaiselle La7-televisiokanavalle antamassaan puhelinhaastattelussa, että Meloni olisi anellut päästä yhteiskuvaan hänen kanssaan. Kanava ei julkaissut Trumpin alkuperäisiä englanninkielisiä sanoja, vaan haastattelu selostettiin italiaksi.

Meloni vastasi väitteeseen Instagram-videolla ja sanoi olevansa siitä vilpittömästi hämmästynyt. Hän sanoi, ettei ymmärrä, miksi Yhdysvaltain presidentti käyttäytyy tällä tavoin liittolaisia kohtaan, ja lisäsi, ettei kyse hänen mukaansa ollut ensimmäisestä vastaavasta tapauksesta.

Trump palasi aiheeseen Truth Social -palvelussa ja toisti väitteensä, että Italian pääministeri olisi pyytänyt kuvaa yhä uudelleen. Samassa kirjoituksessa hän arvosteli Melonia myös Iran-politiikasta ja syytti tätä siitä, ettei Italia tukenut Yhdysvaltain pyrkimyksiä estää Irania hankkimasta tai kehittämästä ydinaseita.

## Italian hallitus puolusti pääministeriä

Italian hallitus asettui perjantaina Melonin tueksi ja tuomitsi Trumpin väitteet. Ulkoministeri Antonio Tajani perui äkillisesti viikonlopuksi suunnitellun matkansa Yhdysvaltoihin ja kuvasi Trumpin puheita vakaviksi ja loukkaaviksi Melonia sekä koko Italiaa kohtaan.

Italian ulkoministeriö ilmoitti myöhemmin, että myös Miamissa järjestettäväksi suunniteltu liike-elämän ja tieteen foorumi, johon Tajani oli määrä osallistua, peruttiin.

Trump väitti lisäksi, että Meloni olisi aiheuttanut merkittävää logistista haittaa estämällä Yhdysvaltoja käyttämästä Italian lentotukikohtia amerikkalaisiin sotilasoperaatioihin Iranissa. Hän myös väitti Melonin suosion olevan Italiassa heikko.

Meloni puolestaan arvosteli Trumpia siitä, ettei tämä hänen mukaansa osoita yhtä päättäväistä linjaa lännen ja Yhdysvaltain vastustajia kohtaan kuin liittolaisiaan kohtaan. Kiista osuu herkkään kohtaan, sillä Italia on pitkään ollut Yhdysvaltain keskeinen eurooppalainen liittolainen.
summary_bullets: Trump toisti väitteensä, että Meloni olisi pyytänyt yhteiskuvaa G7-kokouksessa useaan otteeseen.
Meloni torjui väitteen ja sanoi olevansa siitä hämmästynyt.
Italian ulkoministeri Antonio Tajani perui Yhdysvaltain-matkansa Trumpin kommenttien jälkeen.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu packetin neljään lähdeblokkiin. La7-haastattelun osalta huomioitu, ettei alkuperäisiä englanninkielisiä sanoja julkaistu vaan ne selostettiin italiaksi.

Credit: AP/Mandel Ngan ROME — The Italian government closed ranks on Friday to slam U.S. President Donald Trump over his claim that Premier Giorgia Meloni had “begged” for a photo with him during the recent G7 summit, a pushback that suggested America’s longtime European ally had had enough of Trump’s boasting and criticism. Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani abruptly cancelled a planned trip to the United States this weekend, calling Trump’s claims “serious and offensive” toward Meloni and all of Italy. The Foreign Ministry later announced that the business and scientific forum Tajani was to attend in Miami had also been called off.

But soon afterwards, Trump gave a phone interview with Italy's La7 TV channel in which he alleged: "She begged me to take a photo with her; I felt sorry for her." "She's probably happy I spoke to her," he said. La7 did not produce Trump's original words in English, but voiced them over in Italian. Responding to the claim, Meloni in an Instagram video said she was "frankly stunned". "I don't know why the US president behaves this way towards allies," she said, adding it was not the first time it had happened. "I can only say it is regrettable he does not show the same determination towards the enemies of the West and towards the enemies of the US - [enemies] whose leaders he instead appears to be far more accommodating with."
